name: design-screen-drill
title: Fifteen-minute system design rehearsal
description: A compressed rehearsal of a fifteen-minute design conversation, with answer-aloud pauses and one uninterrupted final answer. It is not a literal interview timer.
authoring_brief: Open with a concrete customer-visible failure. Play a realistic fifteen-minute interview in compressed audio: the candidate asks useful questions, states a measurable contract, gives an API and data flow, and adapts to exactly two changed requirements. The interviewer pushes back on a plausible incomplete answer. No candidate monologue exceeds about two hundred words. Insert a real pause after at least two prompts so the listener answers before the model response. End with one uninterrupted, concise interview answer and a three-beat recall cue. The scenarios are original practice, not predictions of an employer's questions or production architecture.

sections.title: The customer consequence
sections.brief: Start with the customer-visible failure before naming a technology.

sections.title: Ask, then bound the problem
sections.brief: Interviewer poses the problem. Candidate asks two or three high-value clarifications, then repeats the contract.

sections.title: The first workable design
sections.brief: Concrete API, tables or keys, and one write and read flow. Tie choices to requirements.

sections.title: First change
sections.brief: Interviewer introduces a failure or changed constraint. Let the listener answer aloud, then candidate repairs the exact broken invariant.

sections.title: Second change
sections.brief: A different pressure tests adaptation. Name the customer impact and tradeoff.

sections.title: Say the whole answer
sections.brief: A single uninterrupted candidate answer in a few spoken beats, suitable for shadowing aloud.

sections.title: Recall without the script
sections.brief: Ask the listener to retrieve three anchors, leave a real pause, then give a brief cue and next action.
